abstract: We explore the relationship between polynomial functors and (rooted) trees. In the first part, we use polynomial functors to derive a new convenient formalism for trees, and obtain a natural and conceptual construction of the category Ω of Moerdijk and Weiss; its main properties are described in terms of some factorization systems. Although the constructions are motivated and explained in terms of polynomial functors, they all amount to elementary manipulations with finite sets. In the second part, we describe polynomial endofunctors and monads as structures built from trees, characterizing the images of several nerve functors from polynomial endofunctors and monads into presheaves on categories of trees. Polynomial endofunctors and monads over a base are characterized by a sheaf condition on categories of decorated trees. In the absolute case, one further condition is needed, a certain projectivity condition, which serves also to characterize polynomial endofunctors and monads among (colored) collections and operads.

articleTitle: Correlation and Brascamp–Lieb Inequalities for Markov Semigroups
abstract: This paper builds upon several recent works, where semigroup proofs of Brascamp–Lieb inequalities are provided in various settings (Euclidean space, spheres, and symmetric groups). Our aim is two-fold. Firstly, we provide a general, unifying, framework based on Markov generators, in order to cover a variety of examples of interest going beyond previous investigations. Secondly, we put forward the combinatorial reasons for which unexpected exponents occur in these inequalities. Related superadditivity of information and entropy inequalities are also studied.

For functions that take values in the Clifford algebra, we study the Clifford–Fourier transform on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^m$</tex> defined with a kernel function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\ (x,\ y):=e^{\frac{{\mathrm i}\pi}{2}\Gamma_{\underline y}}\ {\mathrm e}^{-{\mathrm i}\langle\underline x,\underline y\rangle}$</tex>, replacing the kernel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{{\mathrm i}\langle\underline x,\underline y\rangle}$</tex> of the ordinary Fourier transform, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\underline y}:=-\Sigma_{j< k}e_je_k(y_j\partial_{y_k}-Y_k\partial_{y_j})$</tex>. An explicit formula of K(x,y) is derived, which can be further simplified to a finite sum of Bessel functions when m is even. The closed formula of the kernel allows us to study the Clifford–Fourier transform and prove the inversion formula, for which a generalized translation operator and a convolution are defined and used.

articleTitle: Action-angle Coordinates for Integrable Systems on Poisson Manifolds
abstract: We prove the action-angle theorem in the general context of non-commutative integrable systems on Poisson manifolds. It implies the existence of action-angle coordinates for Liouville integrable systems on Poisson manifolds, a generalization of the classical result, which is stated in the context of symplectic manifolds. The proof uses the calculus of polyvector fields, rather than differential forms, in particular, we use in the end a Poisson version of the classical Carathéodory–Jacobi–Lie theorem, which we also prove.

articleTitle: Uniform Asymptotics for Discrete Orthogonal Polynomials with Respect to Varying Exponential Weights on a Regular Infinite Lattice
abstract: We consider the large N asymptotics of a system of discrete orthogonal polynomials on an infinite regular lattice of mesh N1/N, with weight e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−NV (x)</sup>, where V (x) is a real analytic function with sufficient growth at infinity. The proof is based on the formulation of an interpolation problem for discrete orthogonal polynomials, which can be converted to a Riemann–Hilbert problem, and steepest descent analysis of this Riemann–Hilbert problem.

articleTitle: 2-Auslander Algebras Associated with Reduced Words in Coxeter Groups
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the endomorphism algebras of standard cluster tilting objects in the stably 2-Calabi–Yau categories <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Sub}\ \Lambda _w$</tex> with elements w in Coxeter groups in [4]. They are examples of the 2-Auslander algebras introduced in [12]. Generalizing the work in [9], we show that they are quasihereditary, even strongly quasihereditary in the sense of [18]. We also describe the cluster tilting object giving rise to the Ringel dual and prove that there is a duality between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Sub}\ \Lambda _w$</tex> and the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F\ (\Delta)$</tex> of good modules over the quasihereditary algebra. When w = uv is a reduced word, we show that the 2-Calabi–Yau triangulated category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline{\mathrm Sub}\ \Lambda_v$</tex> is equivalent to a specific subfactor category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline{\mathrm Sub}\ \Lambda_w$</tex>. This is applied to show that a standard cluster tilting object M in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline{\mathrm Sub}\ \Lambda_w$</tex> and the cluster tilting object Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf> ⊕ΩM lie in the same component in the cluster tilting graph.

In this paper, we study Kolyvagin systems, as defined by Mazur and Rubin, over the cyclotomic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z_p$</tex>-tower for a Gal<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Gal}(\bar {\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)$</tex>-representation T. We prove, under certain hypotheses, that the module of Λ-adic Kolyvagin systems for the cyclotomic deformation T⊗Λ is free of rank 1 over the cyclotomic Iwasawa algebra. We link our result with a web of conjectures due to Perrin-Riou and Rubin; and we relate the Λ-adic Kolyvagin systems we prove to exist to (conjectural) p-adic L-functions. We also study the Iwasawa theory of Rubin–Stark elements via the perspective offered by our main theorem, and outline a strategy to deduce the main conjectures of Iwasawa theory for totally real number fields assuming the Rubin–Stark conjecture.

articleTitle: Analyticity of the Streamlines for Periodic Traveling Water Waves with Bounded Vorticity
abstract: We prove that the streamlines underneath the surface of a periodic traveling water wave propagating above a flat bed with constant speed which exceeds the horizontal velocity of all fluid particles are real analytic provided the vorticity function is merely bounded and measurable.

articleTitle: The Heat Semigroup in the Compact Heckman–Opdam Setting and the Segal–Bargmann Transform
abstract: In the first part of this paper, we study the heat equation and the heat kernel associated with the Heckman–Opdam Laplacian in the compact, Weyl-group invariant setting. In particular, this Laplacian gives rise to a Feller–Markov semigroup on a fundamental alcove of the affine Weyl group. The second part of the paper is devoted to the Segal–Bargmann transform in our context. A Hilbert space of holomorphic functions is defined such that the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-heat transform becomes a unitary isomorphism.

articleTitle: Notes on Kontsevich–Soibelman’s Theorem about Cyclic A∞-algebras
abstract: Kontsevich and Soibelman have proved a relation between a nondegenerate cyclic homology element of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_\infty$</tex>-algebra A and its cyclic inner products on the minimal model of A. We find an explicit formula of this correspondence, in terms of the strong homotopy inner products and negative cyclic cohomology of A. We prove that an equivalence class of the induced strong homotopy inner product depends only on the given negative cyclic cohomology class. Also, we extend such a correspondence to the case of gapped filtered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_\infty$</tex>-algebras.

articleTitle: Recursive Formulas for Welschinger Invariants of the Projective Plane
abstract: Welschinger invariants of the real projective plane can be computed via the enumeration of enriched graphs, called marked floor diagrams. By a purely combinatorial study of these objects, we establish a Caporaso–Harris type formula which allows one to compute Welschinger invariants for configurations of points with any number of complex conjugated points.

A simple characterization of topological amenability in terms of bounded cohomology is proved, following Johnson’s formulation of amenability. The connection to injective Banach modules is established.

articleTitle: The Direct Sum Map on Grassmannians and Jeu de Taquin for Increasing Tableaux
abstract: The direct sum map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Gr}(a,\ \mathbb C^n)\ \times\ {\mathrm Gr}(b,\ \mathbb C^m)\rightarrow {\mathrm Gr}(a+b, \mathbb C^{m+n})$</tex> on Grassmannians induces a K-theory pullback that defines the splitting coefficients. We geometrically explain an identity from Buch [“Grothendieck classes of quiver varieties.” Duke Mathematical Journal 115, no. 1 (2002): 75–103] between the splitting coefficients and the Schubert structure constants for products of Schubert structure sheaves. This is related to the topic of product and splitting coefficients for Schubert boundary ideal sheaves. Our main results extend jeu de taquin for increasing tableaux [Thomas and Yong. “A jeu de taquin theory for increasing tableaux, with applications to K-theoretic Schubert calculus.” Algebra and Number Theory Journal 3, no. 2 (2009): 121–48] by proving transparent analogues of Schützenberger’s [“La Correspondance de Robinson.” In Combinatoire et Représentation du Groupe Symétrique (Strasbourg, 1976), edited by D. Foata, 59–113. Lecture Notes in Mathematics 579. Berlin: Springer, 1977] fundamental theorems on well definedness of rectification. We then establish that jeu de taquin gives rules for each of these four kinds of coefficients.

articleTitle: On a Spectral Analog of the Strong Multiplicity One Theorem
abstract: We prove spectral analogs of the classical strong multiplicity one theorem for newforms. Let Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> be uniform lattices in a semisimple group G. Suppose all but finitely many irreducible unitary representations (resp. spherical) of G occur with equal multiplicities in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>\G) and L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>\G). Then L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>\G)≅L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>\G) as G modules (resp. the spherical spectra of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>\G) and L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>\G) are equal).
Fields that are complete with respect to an absolute value or a valuation of finite rank are known to be ample. We construct complete valued fields that are not ample.

articleTitle: Eigenfunction Localization for the 2D Periodic Schrödinger Operator
abstract: We prove that for any fixed trigonometric polynomial potential satisfying a genericity condition, the spectrum of the two-dimensional periodic Schrödinger operator has finite multiplicity and the Fourier series of the eigenfunctions are uniformly exponentially localized about a finite number of frequencies. As a corollary, the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> norms of the eigenfunctions are bounded for all p > 0, which answers a question of Toth and Zelditch [15].

articleTitle: Periodic Bounce Orbits of Prescribed Energy
abstract: We prove the existence of periodic bounce orbits of prescribed energy on an open bounded domain in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^N$</tex>. We derive explicit bounds on the period and the number of bounce points.

Donaldson introduced an interesting geometric structure (the Donaldson metric) on the space of volume forms for any compact Riemannian manifold, which has nonpositive sectional curvature formally. The geodesic equation and its perturbed equations are fully nonlinear elliptic equations. These equations are also equivalent to two free boundary problems of the Laplacian equation, and it also has a relationship with many interesting problems, such as Nahm's equation. In this paper, we solve these equations and demonstrate the geometric structure of the space of volume forms; in particular, we show that the space of volume forms with the Donaldson metric is a metric space with non-positive curvature in Alexanderov sense.

articleTitle: Isospectral Problem of Locally Symmetric Spaces
abstract: The purpose of this note is to provide answers to two questions raised by Prasad and Rapinchuk in their study of isospectral symmetric spaces.

articleTitle: Long-Time Asymptotics for Solutions of the NLS Equation with a Delta Potential and Even Initial Data
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) with a delta potential and even initial data. The problem is equivalent to the solution of the initial/boundary problem for NLS on a half-line with Robin boundary conditions at the origin. We follow the method of Bikbaev and Tarasov which utilizes a Bäcklund transformation to extend the solution on the half-line to a solution of the NLS equation on the whole line. We study the asymptotic stability of the stationary 1-soliton solution of the equation under perturbation by applying the nonlinear steepest-descent method for Riemann–Hilbert problems introduced by Deift and Zhou. Our work strengthens, and extends, the earlier work on the problem by Holmer and Zworski.

Let G be a semisimple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. In this note, we show that every regular face of the Littlewood–Richardson cone of G gives rise to a reduction rule: a rule which, given a problem “on that face” of computing the multiplicity of an irreducible component in a tensor product, reduces it to a similar problem on a group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar G$</tex> of smaller rank.

articleTitle: Distinguished Generic Representations of GL(n) over p-adic Fields
abstract: Let K/F be a quadratic extension of p-adic fields, and n a positive integer. A smooth irreducible representation of the group GL(n, K) is said to be distinguished, if it admits on its space a nonzero GL(n, F)-invariant linear form. In the present work, we classify distinguished generic representations of the group GL(n, K) in terms of inducing quasi-square-integrable representations. This has, as a consequence, the truth of the expected equality between the Rankin–Selberg type Asai L-function of a generic representation and the Asai L-function of its Langlands parameter.

articleTitle: Deformations of Orbifolds with Noncommutative Linear Poisson Structures
abstract: Let Γ be a finite group acting faithfully and linearly on a real vector space V . Let T(V <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup>) (S(V <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup>)) be the tensor (symmetric) algebra associated to V <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup> which has a natural Γ action. We study generalized quadratic relations on the tensor algebra T(V <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup>) ⋊ Γ. We prove that the quotient algebras of T(V <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup>) ⋊ Γ by such relations satisfy the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt (PBW) property. Such quotient algebras can be viewed as quantizations of linear or constant Poisson structures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(V^*)\rtimes \Gamma$</tex>, and are natural generalizations of symplectic reflection algebras. We study these algebras via various examples and their related cohomologies.

articleTitle: On the Largest Eigenvalue of a Hermitian Random Matrix Model with Spiked External Source I. Rank 1 Case
abstract: Consider a Hermitian matrix model under an external potential with spiked external source. When the external source is of rank 1, we compute the limiting distribution of the largest eigenvalue for general, regular, analytic potential for all values of the external source. There is a transitional phenomenon, which is universal for convex potentials. However, for nonconvex potentials, new types of transition may occur. The higher rank external source is analyzed in the subsequent paper.

articleTitle: Algebraic Group Analogues of the Slodowy Slices and Deformations of Poisson W-algebras
abstract: We define algebraic group analogues of the Slodowy transversal slices to adjoint orbits in a complex semisimple Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>. The new slices are transversal to the conjugacy classes in an algebraic group G with Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>. These slices are associated to (the conjugacy classes of) elements s of the Weyl group W of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>. For such slices, we prove an analogue of the Kostant cross-section theorem for the action of a unipotent group. Using this theorem, we equip the new slices with certain Poisson structures obtained by Poisson reduction from a Poisson–Lie group structure on G.

articleTitle: The Wronski Map and Shifted Tableau Theory
abstract: The Mukhin–Tarasov–Varchenko theorem, conjectured by B. and M. Shapiro, has a number of interesting consequences. Among them is a well-behaved correspondence between certain points on a Grassmannian—those sent by the Wronski map to polynomials with only real roots—and (dual equivalence classes of) Young tableaux. In this paper, we restrict this correspondence to the orthogonal Grassmannian OG(n,2n+1)⊂Gr(n,2n+1). We prove that a point lies on OG(n,2n+1) if and only if the corresponding tableau has a certain type of symmetry. From this, we recover much of the theory of shifted tableaux for Schubert calculus on OG(n,2n+1), including a new, geometric proof of the Littlewood–Richardson rule for OG(n,2n+1).

articleTitle: A Quantum Cluster Algebra of Kronecker Type and the Dual Canonical Basis
abstract: The article concerns the dual of Lusztig’s canonical basis of a subalgebra of the positive part <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak n)$</tex> of the quantized universal enveloping algebra of a Kac–Moody Lie algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^{(1)}_1$</tex>. The examined subalgebra is associated with a terminal module M over the path algebra of the Kronecker quiver via a Weyl group element w of length 4. Geiß–Leclerc–Schröer attached to M a category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal C_M$</tex> of nilpotent modules over the preprojective algebra of the Kronecker quiver together with an acyclic cluster algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A(\mathcal C_M)$</tex>. The dual semicanonical basis contains all cluster monomials. By construction, the cluster algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A(\mathcal C_M)$</tex> is a subalgebra of the graded dual of the (nonquantized) universal enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak n)$</tex>. We transfer to the quantized setup. Following Lusztig, we attach to w a subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U^+_q(w)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak n)$</tex>. The subalgebra is generated by four elements that satisfy straightening relations; it degenerates to a commutative algebra in the classical limit q = 1. The algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U^+_q(w)$</tex> possesses four bases, a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt basis, a canonical basis, and their duals. We prove recursions for dual canonical basis elements. The recursions imply that every cluster variable in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A(\mathcal C_M)$</tex> is the specialization of the dual of an appropriate canonical basis element. Therefore, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U^+_q(w)$</tex> is a quantum cluster algebra in the sense of Berenstein–Zelevinsky. Furthermore, we give explicit formulae for the quantized cluster variables and for expansions of products of dual canonical basis elements.

articleTitle: GIT Compactifications of ℳ0,n from Conics
abstract: We study geometric invariant theory (GIT) quotients parameterizing n-pointed conics that generalize the GIT quotients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb P^1)^n//{\mathrm SL}_2$</tex>. Our main result is that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\mathcal M}_{0,n}$</tex> admits a morphism to each such GIT quotient, generalizing the well-known result of Kapranov for the simpler <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb P^1)^n$</tex> quotients. Moreover, these morphisms factor through Hassett’s moduli spaces of weighted pointed rational curves, where the weight data comes from the GIT linearization data.

articleTitle: Erratum: Three combinatorial models for $\widehat {{\mathrm sl}}_n$ crystals, with applications to cylindric plane partitions
A Combinatorial Description of the U2=0 Version of Heegaard Floer Homology
abstract: We show that every 3-manifold admits a Heegaard diagram in which a truncated version of Heegaard Floer homology (when the holomorphic disks pass through the base points at most once) can be computed combinatorially.

For an arbitrary curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z\subset \mathbb P^3$</tex> (possibly reducible, non-reduced, of mixed dimension) lying on a normal surface, the general surface S of high degree containing Z is also normal but often singular. We compute the class groups of the very general such surface, thereby extending the Noether–Lefschetz theorem (the special case when Z is empty). Our method is an adaptation of Griffiths and Harris’ degeneration proof, simplified by a cohomology and base change argument. We give applications to computing Picard groups. Dedicated to Robin Hartshorne on his 70th birthday

articleTitle: On Injective Modules and Support Varieties for the Small Quantum Group
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex> be the small quantum group at a root of unity associated to a simple Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>. Generalizing a classical result for algebraic groups, we show that if M is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex>-module admitting a compatible torus action, then the injectivity of M can be detected by the restriction of M to certain root subalgebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex>. We provide two proofs of this fact. The first is combinatorial and applies also to the higher Frobenius–Lusztig kernels of the big quantum group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex> containing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex>. The second proof is geometric and makes use of a new rank-variety-type result for the Borel subalgebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_\zeta\ (\mathfrak g)$</tex>. A brief application of the new rank variety result is also discussed.

articleTitle: On the Distribution of Extreme Values of Zeta and L-Functions in the Strip ½ < σ < 1
abstract: We study the distribution of large (and small) values of several families of L-functions on a line Re(s)=σ, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {1}{2}<\sigma< 1$</tex>. We consider the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) in the t-aspect, Dirichlet L-functions in the q-aspect, and L-functions attached to primitive holomorphic cusp forms of weight 2 in the level aspect. For each family, we show that the L-values can be very well modeled by an adequate random Euler product, uniformly in a wide range. We also prove new Ω-results for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions (predicted to be best possible by the probabilistic model) conditionally on generalized Riemann hypothesis, and other results related to large moments of ζ(σ+it).

articleTitle: Small Gaps Between Almost Primes, the Parity Problem, and Some Conjectures of Erdős on Consecutive Integers
abstract: In a previous paper, the authors proved that in any system of three linear forms satisfying obvious necessary local conditions, there are at least two forms that infinitely often assume E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-values; that is, values that are products of exactly two primes. We use this result to prove that there are infinitely many positive integers x such that both x and x + 1 have prime factorizations of the form p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. Consequently, there are infinitely many integers x that simultaneously satisfy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega (x) = \omega (x + 1) = 4,\ \Omega (x) = \Omega (x + 1) = 5, {\mathrm and}\ d(x) = d(x + 1) = 24$</tex>. We prove several other similar theorems. Our results sharpen earlier works by Heath-Brown and Schlage-Puchta.

articleTitle: Unipotent Flows and Isotropic Quadratic Forms in Positive Characteristic
abstract: The analogous statement to Oppenheim conjecture over a local field of positive characteristic is proved. The dynamical argument is most involved in the case of characteristic 3.

articleTitle: A Priori Estimates for Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flows
abstract: We derive a priori estimates for solutions of Lagrangian mean curvature flows. A Liouville-type result for ancient solutions is also obtained in the course of the arguments.

articleTitle: Quantum Cluster Algebra Structures on Quantum Grassmannians and their Quantum Schubert Cells: The Finite-type Cases
abstract: We exhibit quantum cluster algebra structures on quantum Grassmannians <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb K_q[{\mathrm Gr}(2,n)]$</tex> and their quantum Schubert cells, as well as on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb K_q[{\mathrm Gr}(3,\ 6))],\ \mathbb K_q[{\mathrm Gr}(3,\ 7)]$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb K_q[{\mathrm Gr}(3,\ 8)]$</tex>. These cases are precisely those where the quantum cluster algebra is of finite type, and the structures we describe quantize those found by Scott for the classical situation.

articleTitle: Dynamics of KdV Solitons in the Presence of a Slowly Varying Potential
abstract: We study the dynamics of solitons as solutions to the perturbed KdV (pKdV) equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial_tu=-\partial_x(\partial^2_xu+3u^2-bu)$</tex>, where b(x,t)=b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(hx, ht), h≪1, is a slowly varying, but not small, potential. We obtain an explicit description of the trajectory of the soliton parameters of scale and position on the dynamically relevant time scale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta \ h^{-1}\ {\mathrm log}\ h^{-1}$</tex>, together with an estimate on the error of size h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>. In addition to the Lyapunov analysis commonly applied to these problems, we use a local virial estimate due to Martel and Merle “Asymptotic stability of solitons for subcritical gKdV equations revisited.” Nonlinearity 18 (2005): 55–80. The results are supported by numerics. The proof does not rely on the inverse scattering machinery and is expected to carry through for the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> subcritical gKdV-p equation, 1<p<5.

articleTitle: Free Basis Consisting of Strictly Small Sections
abstract: Let X be a projective arithmetic variety and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline L$</tex> a continuous hermitian invertible sheaf on X. In this paper, we would like to consider a mild and appropriate condition to guarantee that H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(X, nL) has a free basis consisting of strictly small sections for n ≫1.

articleTitle: Characterization of Standard Embeddings between Rational Homogeneous Manifolds of Picard Number 1
abstract: Let X be a rational homogeneous manifold of Picard number 1. A subdiagram of the marked Dynkin diagram of X induces naturally an embedding of a rational homogeneous manifold Z into X. By a standard embedding of Z into X we will mean the composite of it with the action of an element of Aut<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(X). In this paper, we prove a characterization of standard embeddings of Z into X by means of varieties of minimal rational tangents in the case where Z is nonlinear. We also provide a characterization of maximal linear spaces in X.

articleTitle: Embedded Cobordism Categories and Spaces of Submanifolds
abstract: Galatius, Madsen, Tillmann, and Weiss [7] have identified the homotopy type of the classifying space of the cobordism category with objects (d −1)-dimensional manifolds embedded in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>. In this paper we apply the techniques of spaces of manifolds, as developed by the author and Galatius in [8], to identify the homotopy type of the cobordism category with objects (d −1)-dimensional submanifolds of a fixed background manifold M. There is a description in terms of a space of sections of a bundle over M associated to its tangent bundle. This can be interpreted as a form of Poincaré duality, relating a space of submanifolds of M to a space of functions on M.

articleTitle: Binomial Coefficients and Littlewood–Richardson Coefficients for Jack Polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we consider translation and multiplication operators acting on the rings of symmetric and nonsymmetric polynomials and study their matrix coefficients with respect to the bases of Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials. The main new insight is that the symmetric and nonsymmetric cases share a key combinatorial feature, that of a locally finite graded poset with a minimum element. This allows us to treat both cases in a simple and unified manner.

articleTitle: Quantitative Density under Higher Rank Abelian Algebraic Toral Actions
abstract: We generalize Bourgain–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh’s recent one-dimensional quantitative density result to abelian algebraic actions of rank at least 2 on higher dimensional tori. Up to finite index, the group actions that we study are conjugate to the action of U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>, the group of units of some non-CM number field K, on a compact quotient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\otimes _\mathbb Q\mathbb R$</tex>. In such a setting, we investigate how fast the orbit of a generic point can become dense in the torus. This effectivizes a special case of a theorem of Berend; and is deduced from a parallel measure-theoretical statement which effectivizes a special case of a result by Katok–Spatzier. In addition, we specify two numerical invariants of the group action that determine the quantitative behavior, which have number-theoretical significance.

articleTitle: On the Fourth Moment of the Riemann Zeta Function
abstract: Applying the approach of multiple Dirichlet series, we recover the classical fourth moment of the Riemann zeta function, but avoid the delicate analysis of “shifted divisor sums”. This work supplements the author’s previous work on the integral mean value of cuspidal automorphic forms over GL(2).

articleTitle: String, Dilaton, and Divisor Equation in Symplectic Field Theory
abstract: Infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems appear naturally in the rich algebraic structure of symplectic field theory. Carefully defining a generalization of gravitational descendants and adding them to the picture, one can produce an infinite number of symmetries of such systems. As in Gromov–Witten theory, the study of the topological meaning of gravitational descendants yields new differential equations for the SFT Hamiltonian, where the key point is to understand the dependence of the algebraic constructions on choices of auxiliary data such as differential forms representing cohomology classes on the target and coherent collections of sections used to define gravitational descendants.

articleTitle: Wave Breaking and Global Existence for a Generalized Two-Component Camassa–Holm System
abstract: In this paper, we study a generalized two-component Camassa–Holm system which can be derived from the theory of shallow water waves moving over a linear shear flow. This new system also generalizes a class of dispersive waves in cylindrical compressible hyperelastic rods. We show that this new system can still exhibit the wave-breaking phenomenon. We also determine the exact blow-up rate of such solutions. In addition, we establish a sufficient condition for global solutions.

articleTitle: Complexity and Module Varieties for Classical Lie Superalgebras
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g_{\bar 0}\oplus \mathfrak g_{\bar 1}$</tex> be a classical Lie superalgebra and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex> be the category of finite-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>-supermodules which are semisimple over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g_{\bar 0}$</tex>. In this paper we investigate the homological properties of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex>. In particular, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex> is self-injective in the sense that all projective supermodules are injective. We also show that all supermodules in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex> admit a projective resolution with polynomial rate of growth, and, hence, one can study complexity in ℱ. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> is a type I Lie superalgebra, we introduce support varieties which detect projectivity and are related to the associated varieties of Duflo and Serganova. With this new approach, we prove that the conditions of being tilting or projective are equivalent for type I Lie superalgebras.

articleTitle: There is a Unique Real Tight Contact 3-Ball
abstract: We prove that there is a unique real tight contact structure on the 3-ball with convex boundary up to isotopy through real tight contact structures. We also give a partial classification of the real tight solid tori with the real structure being antipodal map along longitudinal and the identity along meridional direction. For the proofs, we use the real versions of contact neighborhood theorems and the invariant convex surface theory in real contact manifolds.

articleTitle: Free Biholomorphic Classification of Noncommutative Domains
abstract: In this paper, we develop a theory of free holomorphic functions on noncommutative Reinhardt domains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^m_f(\mathcal H)\subset B(\mathcal H)^n$</tex>, generated by positive regular free holomorphic functions f in n noncommuting variables and by positive integers m ≥ 1, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(\mathcal H)$</tex> is the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H$</tex>. Noncommutative Berezin transforms are used to study Hardy algebras H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>) and domain algebras A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>) associated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^m_f(\mathcal H)$</tex> and compositions of free holomorphic functions. We obtain noncommutative Cartan type results for formal power series, in several noncommuting indeterminates, which leave invariant the nilpotent parts of the corresponding domains. As a consequence, we characterize the set of all free biholomorphic functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F:{\mathrm D}^m_f(\mathcal H)\rightarrow {\mathrm D}^l_g(\mathcal H)$</tex> with F(0) = 0. We show that the free biholomorphic classification of the domains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}^m_f(\mathcal H)$</tex> is the same as the classification, up to unital completely isometric isomorphisms having completely contractive hereditary extension, of the corresponding noncommutative domain algebras A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>). In particular, we prove that Ψ : A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) → A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) is a unital completely isometric isomorphism if and only if there is a free biholomorphic map φ ∈ Bih(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\Psi(\chi)=\chi\circ\varphi,\qquad\chi\in A({\mathrm D}^1_{f,{\mathrm rad}}).$$</tex> This implies that the noncommutative domains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}^1_f(\mathcal H)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}^1_g(\mathcal H)$</tex> are free biholomorphic equivalent if and only if the domain algebras A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) and A(D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g, rad</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) are completely isometrically isomorphic. Using the interaction between the theory of functions in several complex variables and our noncommutative theory, we provide several results concerning the free biholomorphic classification of the noncommutative domains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}^m_f(\mathcal H)$</tex> and the classification, up to completely isometric isomorphisms, of the associated noncommutative domain (resp. Hardy) algebras. In particular, we characterize the unit ball of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(\mathcal H)^n$</tex> among the noncommutative domains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}^m_f(\mathcal H)$</tex>, up to free biholomorphisms. We also obtain characterizations for the unitarily implemented isomorphisms of noncommutative Hardy (resp. domain) algebras in terms of free biholomorphic functions between the corresponding noncommutative domains.

articleTitle: Baric Structures on Triangulated Categories and Coherent Sheaves
abstract: We introduce the notion of a baric structure on a triangulated category, as an abstraction of S. Morel’s weight truncation formalism for mixed ℓ-adic sheaves. We study these structures on the derived category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D^{\mathrm b}_G\ (X)$</tex> of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on a G-scheme X. Our main result shows how to endow this derived category with a family of nontrivial baric structures when G acts on X with finitely many orbits. We also describe a general construction for producing a new t-structure on a triangulated category equipped with given t- and baric structures, and we prove that the staggered t-structures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D^{\mathrm b}_G\ (X)$</tex> introduced by Achar arise in this way.

articleTitle: Resonance Varieties Via Blowups of ℙ2 and Scrolls
abstract: Conjectures of Suciu [“Fundamental groups of line arrangements: Enumerative aspects,” 43–79. Contemporary Mathematics 276. Providence, RI: American Mathematical Society, 2001.] relate the fundamental group of an arrangement complement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M= \mathbb{C}^{n} {\backslash} \, {\cal A}$</tex> to the first resonance variety of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^*(M, \mathbb{Z})$</tex>. We describe a connection between the first resonance variety and the Orlik–Terao algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C (\cal A)$</tex> of the arrangement. In particular, we show that nonlocal components of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^1 (\cal A)$</tex> give rise to determinantal syzygies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C (\cal A)$</tex>. As a result, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C (\cal A)$</tex> lies on a scroll, placing geometric constraints on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^1 (\cal A)$</tex>. The key observation is that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C (\cal A)$</tex> is the homogeneous coordinate ring associated to a nef but not an ample divisor on the blowup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^2$</tex> at the singular points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {A}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Integer Matrix Exact Covering Systems and Product Identities for Theta Functions
abstract: In this paper, we prove that there is a natural correspondence between product identities for Ramanujan’s theta functions and integer matrix exact covering systems. We show that since <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}^{n}$</tex> can be taken as the disjoint union of a lattice generated by n linearly independent vectors in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}^{n}$</tex> and a finite number of its translates, certain products of theta functions can be written as linear combinations of other products of theta functions. We first give a general theorem to write a product of n theta functions as a linear combination of other products of theta functions. Many known identities for products of two theta functions are shown to be special cases of our main theorem. Several entries in Ramanujan’s notebooks as well as new identities are established as applications, including theorems for products of three and four theta functions that have not been obtained by other methods.

articleTitle: A Local Energy Estimate on Kerr Black Hole Backgrounds
abstract: We study dispersive properties for the wave equation in the Kerr space–time with small angular momentum. The main result of this paper is to establish uniform energy bounds and local energy decay for such backgrounds. This follows similar results for the Schwarzschild space–time proved earlier in [3],[8], and [16] and extended in earlier work [29] of the authors and collaborators.

articleTitle: On the Cuspidality of Pullbacks of Siegel Eisenstein Series and Applications to the Bloch–Kato Conjecture
abstract: Let k > 9 be an even integer and p a prime with p > 2k −2. Let f be a newform of weight 2k −2 and level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$</tex> so that f is ordinary at p and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline \rho _{f,\mathfrak p}$</tex> is irreducible. Under some additional hypotheses, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm ord}_p(L_{\mathrm alg}(k,\ f )) \leq {\mathrm ord}p(\#S)$</tex>, where S is the Pontryagin dual of the Selmer group associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho_{f,\mathfrak p}\ \otimes \ \varepsilon^{1-k}$</tex> with ϵ the p-adic cyclotomic character. We accomplish this by first constructing a congruence between the Saito–Kurokawa lift of f and a non-CAP Siegel cusp form. Once this congruence is established, we use Galois representations to obtain the lower bound on the Selmer group.

articleTitle: On Inductive Limits of Type-I C*-Algebras with One-Dimensional Spectrum
abstract: The class of separable C*-algebras which can be written as inductive limits of continuous-trace C*-algebras with spectrum homeomorphic to a disjoint union of trees and trees with a point removed is classified by the Cuntz semigroup.

articleTitle: The Structure of Bivariate Rational Hypergeometric Functions
abstract: We describe the structure of all codimension-2 lattice configurations A which admit a stable rational A-hypergeometric function, that is a rational function F all the partial derivatives of which are nonzero, and which is a solution of the A-hypergeometric system of partial differential equations defined by Gel′ fand, Kapranov, and Zelevinsky. We show, moreover, that all stable rational A-hypergeometric functions may be described by toric residues and apply our results to study the rationality of bivariate series the coefficients of which are quotients of factorials of linear forms.

articleTitle: Projective Reduction of the Discrete Painlevé System of Type (A2 + A1)(1)
abstract: We consider the q-Painlevé III equation arising from the birational representation of the affine Weyl group of type (A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> + A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. We study the reduction of the q-Painlevé III equation to the q-Painlevé II equation from the viewpoint of affine Weyl group symmetry. In particular, the mechanism of apparent inconsistency between the hypergeometric solutions to both equations is clarified by using factorization of difference operators and the τ functions.

articleTitle: Visible Actions on Reducible Multiplicity-Free Spaces
abstract: The notion of (strongly) visible actions was introduced by T. Kobayashi [10,  11] for the biholomorphic action on a complex manifold with (possibly) infinitely many orbits. A holomorphic action of a Lie group G on a complex manifold D is strongly visible with a slice S if D = G ⋅ S, and there exists an anti-holomorphic and orbit preserving diffeomorphism σ on D such that σ|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf> = id<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf>. Generalizing our previous result [22] about strongly visible actions on irreducible multiplicity-free spaces à la Kac, we treat reducible multiplicity-free spaces classified by Benson–Ratcliff and Leahy and prove that any multiplicity-free space naturally admits a strongly visible action. Further, we give an explicit description of S and σ. Our result gives an evidence to Kobayashi's conjecture [12, Conjecture 3.2] in the case of linear actions, asserting that we can take S to have the same dimension with the rank of V.

articleTitle: Note on a Geometric Isogeny of K3 Surfaces
abstract: This paper establishes a correspondence relating two specific classes of complex algebraic K3 surfaces. The first class consists of K3 surfaces polarized by the rank-16 lattice H ⊕ E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> ⊕ E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>. The second class consists of K3 surfaces obtained as minimal resolutions of double covers of the projective plane branched over a configuration of six lines. The correspondence underlies a geometric 2-isogeny of K3 surfaces.

articleTitle: Double Cosets for SU(2) × … × SU(2) and Outer Automorphisms of Free Groups
abstract: Consider the space of double cosets of the product of n copies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm SU}(2)$</tex> with respect to the diagonal subgroup. We get a parametrization of this space, the radial part of the Haar measure, and explicit formulas for the actions of the group of outer automorphisms of the free group F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</inf> and of the braid group of n −1 strings.

articleTitle: Asymptotics for a Determinant with a Confluent Hypergeometric Kernel
abstract: We obtain “large gap” asymptotics for a Fredholm determinant with a confluent hypergeometric kernel. We also obtain asymptotics for determinants with two types of Bessel kernels which appeared in random matrix theory.

articleTitle: Right Coideal Subalgebras of the Borel Part of a Quantized Enveloping Algebra
abstract: For the Borel part of a quantized enveloping algebra, we classify all right coideal subalgebras for which the intersection with the coradical is a Hopf algebra. The result is expressed in terms of characters of the subalgebras U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>[w] of the quantized enveloping algebra, introduced by de Concini, Kac, and Procesi for any Weyl group element w. We explicitly determine all characters of U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>[w] building on recent work by Yakimov on prime ideals of U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>[w] which are invariant under a torus action.

articleTitle: Non-abelian Reciprocity Laws on a Riemann Surface
abstract: On a Riemann surface, there are relations among the periods of holomorphic differential forms called Riemann’s relations. We prove them, using iterated integrals. In this paper, we generalize these relations to relations among generating series of iterated integrals. The generating series gives infinitely many relations—one for each coefficient of the generating series. The lower-order terms give the well-known classical relations. The new result is reciprocity for the higher degree terms, which give non-trivial relations among iterated integrals on a Riemann surface. As an application we refine the definition of Manin’s non-commutative modular symbol in order to include Eisenstein series. Finally, this paper contains some constructions needed for multi-dimensional reciprocity laws like a refinement of one of the Kato–Parshin reciprocity laws (Horozov, I. “A refinement of the Parshin symbol for surfaces”. Preprint, arXiv.org, AG, 1002.2698].

We describe an application of Poincaré duality for completed homology spaces (as defined by Emerton) to level raising for p-adic modular forms. This allows us to give a new description of the image of Chenevier’s p-adic Jacquet–Langlands map between an eigencurve for a definite quaternion algebra and an eigencurve for GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The points on the eigencurve at which we “raise the level” are (nonsmooth) points of intersection between an “old” and a “new” component.

We prove the cyclic formality conjecture for chains, raised by Tsygan [“Formality conjectures for chains.” Differential Topology, Infinite-dimensional Lie Algebras, and Applications 261–74. American Mathematical Society Translation Series 2, 194. Providence, RI: American Mathematical Society, 1999.]. It states the existence of an L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>-quasi-isomorphism of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>-modules between the cyclic chain complex of smooth functions on a manifold and the differential forms on that manifold. Concretely, we prove that the u-linear extension of Shoikhet’s morphism of Hochschild chains [Shoikhet, B. “A proof of the Tsygan formality conjecture for chains.” Advances in Mathematics 179, no. 1 (2003): 7–37.] solves Tsygan’s conjecture.

articleTitle: Tame Galois Realizations of GSp4(𝔽ℓ) over ℚ
abstract: In this paper, we obtain realizations of the 4-dimensional general symplectic group over a prime field of characteristic ℓ > 3 as the Galois group of a tamely ramified Galois extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q$</tex>. The strategy is to consider the Galois representation ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf> attached to the Tate module at ℓ of a suitable abelian surface. We need to choose the abelian surfaces carefully in order to ensure that the image of ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf> is large and simultaneously maintain a control on the ramification of the corresponding Galois extension. We obtain an explicit family of curves of genus 2 such that the Galois representation attached to the ℓ-torsion points of their Jacobian varieties provides tame Galois realizations of the desired symplectic groups.

articleTitle: Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metric Obtains the Minimum of K-energy
abstract: Based on Donaldson's method, we prove that, for an integral Kähler class, when there is a Kähler metric of constant scalar curvature, then it minimizes the K-energy. We do not assume that the automorphism group is discrete.

In this paper, we describe a method to establish when a symplectic manifold M with semi-free Hamiltonian S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-action is unique up to isomorphism (equivariant symplectomorphism). This will rely on a study of the symplectic topology of the reduced spaces. We prove that if the reduced spaces satisfy a rigidity condition, then the manifold M is uniquely determined by fixed point data. In particular, we can prove that there is a unique family up to isomorphism of six-dimensional symplectic manifolds with semi-free S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-action and isolated fixed points.

articleTitle: Lax Formalism for q-Painlevé Equations with Affine Weyl Group Symmetry of Type E(1)n
abstract: An explicit form of the Lax pair for the q-difference Painlevé equation with affine Weyl group symmetry of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^{(1)}_8$</tex> is obtained. Its degeneration to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^{(1)}_7$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^{(1)}_6$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^{(1)}_5$</tex> cases are also given.

articleTitle: Local Asymptotics for Slowly Shrinking Spectral Bands of a Berezin–Toeplitz Operator
abstract: Motivated by geometric quantization, we study how the asymptotics of certain spectral projectors of an invariant self-adjoint Toeplitz operator relate to the full level-k Szegö kernel associated to a positive line bundle on a compact symplectic manifold. These operators quantize classical observables on the “phase space” M, and the semiclassical regime corresponds to k →+∞. We focus on the asymptotics of the spectral projectors of slowly shrinking spectral bands. If “energy” is a zeroth-order Toeplitz operator, then for ξ </2, spectral bands of width O( k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−ξ</sup>) centered at E asymptotically capture all of the Szegö kernel at points of classical energy E. On the same classical locus, these bands also realize a version of Tian's almost isometry.

Our main goal in this paper is to translate the diagram below relating groups, Lie algebras, and Hopf algebras to the corresponding 2-objects, that is, to categorify it. This is done interpreting 2-objects as crossed modules and showing the compatibility of the standard functors linking groups, Lie algebras, and Hopf algebras with the concept of a crossed module. One outcome is the construction of an enveloping algebra of the string Lie algebra of Baez-Crans [Higher-dimensional algebra. VI. Lie 2-algebras. Theory and Applications of Categories 12 (2004): 492–538.], another is the clarification of the passage from crossed modules of Hopf algebras to Hopf 2-algebras.

articleTitle: Moduli of Plane Quartics, Göpel Invariants and Borcherds Products
abstract: It is known that the moduli space of plane quartic curves is birational to an arithmetic quotient of a six-dimensional complex ball [Kondō, S. “A complex hyperbolic structure of the moduli space of curves of genus three.” Journal für die Reine und Angewandte Mathematik 525 (2000): 219–32]. In this paper, we shall show that there exists a 15-dimensional space of meromorphic automorphic forms on the complex ball, which gives a birational embedding of the moduli space of plane quartics with level-2 structure into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^{14}$</tex>. This map coincides with the one given by Coble [“Algebraic geometry and theta functions.” Algebraic geometry and theta functions. American Mathematical Society Colloquium Publication 10. Providence, RI: American Mathematical Society, 1929 (3rd ed., 1969)] by using Göpel invariants.

articleTitle: Suites de Poitou-Tate pour les complexes de tores à deux termes
abstract: On considère un complexe de tores de longueur 2 défini sur un corps de nombres k. On établit des résultats de dualité locale et globale pour l’hypercohomologie (étale ou galoisienne) de ce complexe. On obtient notamment une suite de Poitou-Tate pour de tels complexes, généralisant les suites de Poitou-Tate pour les modules galoisiens finis ou les tores. Les résultats généraux obtenus ici pour les complexes de tores constituent l’ingrédient essentiel dans des résultats récents de l’auteur sur l’approximation forte dans les groupes linéaires connexes et sur des théorèmes de dualité pour la cohomologie galoisienne (non abélienne) de tels groupes. We consider a complex of tori of length 2 defined over a number field k. We establish here some local and global duality theorems for the (étale or Galois) hypercohomology of such a complex. We prove the existence of a Poitou-Tate exact sequence for such a complex, which generalizes the Poitou-Tate exact sequences for finite Galois modules and tori. The general results proven here lie at the root of recent results by the author about the defect of strong approximation in connected linear algebraic groups and about some arithmetic duality theorems for the (non-abelian) Galois cohomology of such groups.

articleTitle: von Neumann Algebras Arising from Bost–Connes Type Systems
abstract: We show that the KMS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">β</inf>-states of Bost–Connes type systems for number fields in the region 0 < β ≤1, as well as of the Connes–Marcolli GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-system for 1 < β ≤2, have type III<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. This is equivalent to ergodicity of various actions on adelic spaces. For example, the case β = 2 of the GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-system corresponds to ergodicity of the action of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℚ) on Mat<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(A) with its Haar measure.

In the present paper, we introduce a quantum analog of the classical folding of a simply laced Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> to the nonsimply laced algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g^\sigma$</tex> along a Dynkin diagram automorphism σ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>. For each quantum folding, we replace <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g^\sigma$</tex> by its Langlands dual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g^{\sigma \vee}$</tex> and construct a nilpotent Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak n$</tex> which interpolates between the nilpotnent parts of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g^{\sigma \vee}$</tex>, together with its quantized enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak n)$</tex> and a Poisson structure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S(\mathfrak n)$</tex>. Remarkably, for the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g^{\sigma \vee})=(\mathfrak {so}_{2n+2}, \mathfrak {sp}_{2n})$</tex>, the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak n)$</tex> admits an action of the Artin braid group Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and contains a new algebra of quantum n×n matrices with an adjoint action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak {sl}_n)$</tex>, which generalizes the algebras constructed by Goodearl and Yakimov in [“Poisson structures on affine spaces and flag varieties. II.” Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 361, no. 11 (2009): 5753–780.]. The hardest case of quantum folding is, quite expectably, the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak {so}_8,\ G_2)$</tex> for which the PBW presentation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak n)$</tex> and the corresponding Poisson bracket on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S(\mathfrak n)$</tex> contains more than 700 terms each.

articleTitle: Systems of Reproducing Kernels and their Biorthogonal: Completeness or Incompleteness?
abstract: Let {v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>} be a complete minimal system in a Hilbert space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H$</tex> and let {w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>} be its biorthogonal system. It is well known that {w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>} is not necessarily complete. However, the situation may change if we consider systems of reproducing kernels in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H$</tex> of analytic functions. We study the completeness problem for a class of spaces with a Riesz basis of reproducing kernels and for model subspaces K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Θ</inf> of the Hardy space. We find a class of spaces where systems biorthogonal to complete systems of reproducing kernels are always complete, and show that in general this is not true. In particular, we answer the question posed by Nikolski and construct a model subspace with an incomplete biorthogonal system.

A simplicial polytope is combinatorially rigid if its combinatorial structure is determined by its graded Betti numbers, which are important invariants coming from combinatorial commutative algebra. We find a necessary condition to be combinatorially rigid for 3-dimensional reducible simplicial polytopes and provide some rigid reducible simplicial polytopes.

We study the notion of positive and negative complexities of pairs of objects in cluster categories. The first main result shows that the maximal complexity occurring is either one, two, or infinite, depending on the representation type of the underlying hereditary algebra. In the second result, we study the bounded derived category of a cluster-tilted algebra, and show that the maximal complexity occurring is either zero or one whenever the algebra is of finite or tame type.

articleTitle: PBW Filtration and Bases for Symplectic Lie Algebras
abstract: We study the PBW filtration on the highest weight representations V (λ) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {sp}_{2n}$</tex>. This filtration is induced by the standard degree filtration on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(n^{-})$</tex>. We give a description of the associated graded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(n^{-})$</tex>-module gr V (λ) in terms of generators and relations. We also construct a basis of gr V (λ). As an application we derive a graded combinatorial formula for the character of V (λ) and obtain a new class of bases of the modules V (λ).

articleTitle: Universality Limits at the Soft Edge of the Spectrum via Classical Complex Analysis
abstract: We show that universality at the soft edge of the spectrum is equivalent to universality “along the diagonal,” that is ratio asymptotics for Christoffel functions. The context is that of varying measures and limits involving the Airy kernel. In particular, we consider measures of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{2n}_n (x)\ {\mathrm d}x$</tex>, where {W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>} are a suitable sequence of weights. They do not need to be analytic, but instead should satisfy some hypotheses on the associated equilibrium measures.

articleTitle: On the Spectral Sequence from Khovanov Homology to Heegaard Floer Homology
abstract: Ozsváth and Szabó [“On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers.” Advances in Mathematics 194, no. 1 (2005): 1–33.] show that there is a spectral sequence the E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> term of which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde {Kh}(L),$</tex> and which converges to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\mathrm HF}(-\Sigma(L))$</tex>. We prove that the E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> term of this spectral sequence is an invariant of the link L for all k≥2. If L is a transverse link in (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>,ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">std</inf>), then we show that Plamenevskaya’s transverse invariant ψ(L) gives rise to a transverse invariant, ψ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>(L), in the E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> term for each k≥2. We use this fact to compute each term in the spectral sequences associated to the torus knots T(3,4) and T(3,5).

articleTitle: Poncelet–Darboux Curves, their Complete Decomposition and Marden Theorem
abstract: Poncelet–Darboux curves are studied. A Poncelet–Darboux curve of degree n−1 is completely decomposable if it consists of (n−1)/2 conics if n is odd; if n is even, completely decomposable curve consists of (n−2)/2 conics and a line. An effective criterion for complete decomposability in terms of pair of polynomials which defines a Poncelet–Darboux curve is derived. A relationship between Poncelet–Darboux curves and the Marden theorem from geometric theory of zeros of polynomial and rational functions is established.

articleTitle: Sup-norms of Eigenfunctions on Arithmetic Ellipsoids
abstract: Let B be a positive quaternion algebra, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr O\subseteq{\mathrm B}$</tex> be an Eichler order. There is associated, in a natural way, a variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X=X(\mathscr O)$</tex> the connected components of which are indexed by the ideal classes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr O$</tex> and are isomorphic to spheres. This variety is naturally equipped with a Laplace operator and a large family of Hecke operators. For a joint eigenfunction φ of the Hecke algebra and of the Laplace operator with eigenvalue λ, the hybrid sup norm bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\parallel\varphi\parallel_{\infty}\ll(tV)^{-\delta}t^{1/2}\parallel\varphi\parallel_2$</tex> for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta < \frac{1}{60}$</tex> is shown, where t=(1+λ)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V={\mathrm vol}(X(\mathscr O))$</tex>.

articleTitle: Skew Littlewood–Richardson Rules from Hopf Algebras
abstract: We use Hopf algebras to prove a version of the Littlewood–Richardson rule for skew Schur functions, which implies a conjecture of Assaf and McNamara. We also establish skew Littlewood–Richardson rules for Schur P- and Q-functions and noncommutative ribbon Schur functions, as well as skew Pieri rules for k-Schur functions, dual k-Schur functions, and for the homology of the affine Grassmannian of the symplectic group.

articleTitle: Gaussian Point Count Statistics for Families of Curves Over a Fixed Finite Field
abstract: We produce a collection of families of curves, whose point count statistics over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_p$</tex> becomes Gaussian for p fixed. In particular, the average number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_p$</tex> points on curves in these families tends to infinity.
