articleTitle: New Lattice Point Asymptotics for Products of Upper Half-planes
abstract: Sadly, Fritz Grunewald died when this work was in the process of revision. We dedicate this paper to his memory. Let Γ be an irreducible lattice in PSL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℝ)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> (d ∈ ℕ) and z a point in the d-fold direct product of the upper half-plane. We study the discrete set of componentwise distances D(Γ, z) ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> defined in (2). We prove asymptotic results on the number of γ ∈Γ such that dist(z, γz) is contained in strips expanding in some directions and also in expanding hypercubes. The results improve the existing error terms, [6], and generalize the best known error term for d = 1, due to Selberg.

We show that the Prym variety associated with a triple covering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:Y\rightarrow X$</tex> of curves is principally polarized of dimension ≥2 if and only if f is noncyclic, étale and X is of genus 2. We investigate some properties of these Prym varieties and their moduli.

For a semistable curve X of genus g, the number h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(X,L) is studied for line bundles L of degree d parameterized by the compactified Picard scheme. The theorem of Riemann is shown to hold. The theorem of Clifford is shown to hold in the following cases: X has two components; X is any semistable curve, and d = 0 or d = 2g − 2; X is stable, free from separating nodes, and d ≤ 4. These results are shown to be sharp. Applications to the Clifford index, to the combinatorial description of hyperelliptic curves, and to plane quintics are given.

articleTitle: Proof of Swiss Cheese Version of Deligne's Conjecture
abstract: For an associative algebra A, we consider the pair “the Hochschild cochain complex C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">•</sup>(A,A) and the algebra A”. There is a natural 2-colored operad which acts on this pair. We show that this operad is quasi-isomorphic to the singular chain operad of Voronov's Swiss Cheese operad. This statement is the Swiss Cheese version of the Deligne conjecture formulated by M. Kontsevich [“Operads and motives in deformation quantization.” Letters in Mathematical Physics 48 (1999) 35–72.].

articleTitle: Complex Hyperbolic Structures on Disc Bundles over Surfaces
abstract: We study complex hyperbolic disc bundles over closed orientable surfaces that arise from discrete and faithful representations H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>→PU(2,1), where H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is the fundamental group of the orbifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{2}(2, \ldots, 2)$</tex> and thus contains a surface group as a subgroup of index 2 or 4. The results obtained provide the first complex hyperbolic disc bundles M→Σ that admit both real and complex hyperbolic structures, satisfy the equality 2(χ+e)=3τ, satisfy the inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{1} \over {2}} \chi < e$</tex>, and induce discrete and faithful representations π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>Σ→PU(2,1) with fractional Toledo invariant, where χ is the Euler characteristic of Σ, e denotes the Euler number of M, and τ stands for the Toledo invariant of M. To obtain a satisfactory explanation of the equality 2(χ+e)=3τ, we conjecture that there exists a holomorphic section in all our examples.In order to reduce the amount of calculations, we systematically explore coordinate-free methods.

articleTitle: Équations multiplicatives sur les sous-variétés des tores
abstract: Given an algebraic subvariety X of a multiplicative torus A over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\mathbb Q}$</tex>, we study the intersection of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X(\bar {\mathbb Q})$</tex> with the union A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[m]</sup> of all algebraic subgroups of codimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m={\mathrm dim}\ X+1$</tex>. This is related to conjectures stated by Zilber and Pink and follows previous work by Bombieri, Masser and Zannier. Our main result can be stated as follows: if X is a nondegenerate subvariety of A, then for any subgroup of finite rank Γ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\bar {\mathbb Q})$</tex>, the points lying in a height-theoretic cone with nonzero radius around ΓA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[m]</sup> are not dense in X. The case Γ={1} was proved by Habegger in 2009 as a corollary to his bounded height theorem. We show here that the general case follows from a new Vojta-type height inequality on X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. The proof of this inequality relies on diophantine approximation techniques coming from previous work by Vojta, Faltings, Bombieri, … , Rémond. It shows that the height inequality can be deduced from a lower bound on some intersection numbers coming from a family of blow-ups of a given compactification of X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. Our main task is to establish this lower bound. For that purpose, we use homogeneity and positivity properties of the intersection numbers. They are proved here in an analytic setting, using integrals of Chern-like forms over suitably chosen desingularizations.

We prove that a closed smooth 4-manifold has shadow-complexity zero if and only if it is a kind of four-dimensional graph manifold, which decomposes into some particular blocks along embedded copies of S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, plus some complex projective spaces. We deduce a classification of all smooth 4-manifolds with finite fundamental group and shadow-complexity zero.

articleTitle: Quasi-Hamiltonian Groupoids and Multiplicative Manin Pairs
abstract: We reformulate notions from the theory of quasi-Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>-manifolds in terms of graded Poisson geometry and graded Poisson–Lie groups and prove that quasi-Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>-manifolds integrate to quasi-Hamiltonian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>-groupoids. We then interpret this result within the theory of Dirac morphisms and multiplicative Manin pairs, to connect our work with more traditional approaches, and also to put it into a wider context suggesting possible generalizations.

articleTitle: Kernel Bundles, Syzygies of Points, and the Effective Cone of Cg−2
abstract: We obtain a complete description of the effective cone of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g−2</inf> when C is a general curve of genus g ≥ 6, as well as a new bound in the case where C is a smooth plane quintic. In addition, we obtain a new virtual bound for the effective cone of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g−2m</inf> which is a genuine bound when m = 2, and we also characterize certain natural divisors on C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g−2</inf> as subordinate loci associated to adjunctions of kernel bundles.

articleTitle: Multi-black Holes and Earthquakes on Riemann Surfaces with Boundaries
abstract: We prove an “Earthquake Theorem” for hyperbolic metrics with geodesic boundary on a compact surface S with boundary: given two hyperbolic metrics with geodesic boundary on a surface with k boundary components, there are 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> right earthquakes transforming the first in the second. An alternative formulation arises by introducing the enhanced Teichmüller space of S: we prove that any two points of the latter are related by a unique right earthquake. The proof rests on the geometry of “multi-black holes,” which are three-dimensional Anti-de Sitter manifolds, topologically the product of a surface with boundary by an interval.

articleTitle: Fibered Transverse Knots and the Bennequin Bound
abstract: We prove that a nicely fibered link (by which we mean the binding of an open book) in a tight contact manifold (M, ξ) with zero Giroux torsion has a transverse representative realizing the Bennequin bound if and only if the contact structure it supports (since it is also the binding of an open book) is ξ. This gives a geometric reason for the non-sharpness of the Bennequin bound for fibered links. We also give the classification, up to contactomorphism, of maximal self-linking number links in these knot types. Moreover, in the standard tight contact structure on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> we classify, up to transverse isotopy, transverse knots with maximal self-linking number in the knot types given as closures of positive braids and given as fibered strongly quasi-positive knots. We derive several braid theoretic corollaries from this. In particular, we give conditions under which quasi-positive braids are related by positive Markov stabilizations and when a minimal braid index representative of a knot is quasi-positive. Finally, we observe that our main result can be used to show, and make rigorous the statement, that contact structures on a given manifold are in a strong sense classified by the transverse knot theory they support.

articleTitle: The Periodic Cauchy Problem for Novikov's Equation
abstract: We study the periodic Cauchy problem for an integrable equation with cubic nonlinearities introduced by Novikov. Like the Camassa–Holm and Degasperis–Procesi equations, Novikov’s equation has Lax pair representations and admits peakon solutions, but it has nonlinear terms that are cubic, rather than quadratic. We show the local well-posedness of the problem in Sobolev spaces and existence and uniqueness of solutions for all time using orbit invariants. Furthermore, we prove a Cauchy–Kowalevski type theorem for this equation, which establishes the existence and uniqueness of real analytic solutions.

articleTitle: Resonances for Manifolds Hyperbolic Near Infinity: Optimal Lower Bounds on Order of Growth
abstract: Suppose that (X, g) is a conformally compact (n+1)-dimensional manifold that is hyperbolic near infinity in the sense that the sectional curvatures of g are identically equal to −1 outside of a compact set K⊂X. We prove that the counting function for the resolvent resonances has maximal order of growth (n+1) generically for such manifolds. This is achieved by constructing explicit examples of manifolds hyperbolic at infinity for which the resonance counting function obeys optimal lower bounds.

articleTitle: The Gradient Flow of the L2 Curvature Energy on Surfaces
abstract: We investigate the gradient flow of the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> norm of the Riemannian curvature on surfaces. We show long-time existence with arbitrary initial data, and exponential convergence of the volume normalized flow to a constant scalar curvature metric when the initial energy is below a constant determined by the Euler characteristic of the underlying surface.

articleTitle: Strongly Solid II1 Factors with an Exotic MASA
abstract: Using an extension of techniques of Ozawa and Popa, we give an example of a non-amenable strongly solid II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> factor M containing an “exotic” maximal abelian subalgebra A: as an A,A-bimodule, L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(M) is neither coarse nor discrete. Thus, we show that there exist II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> factors with such property but without Cartan subalgebras. It also follows from Voiculescu's free entropy results that M is not an interpolated free group factor, yet it is strongly solid and has both the Haagerup property and the complete metric approximation property.

In this note, we study the Koszul–Brylinski homology of holomorphic Poisson manifolds. We show that it is isomorphic to the cohomology of a certain smooth complex Lie algebroid with values in the Evens–Lu–Weinstein duality module. As a consequence, we prove that the Evens–Lu–Weinstein pairing on Koszul–Brylinski homology is nondegenerate. Finally, we compute the Koszul–Brylinski homology for Poisson structures on ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> × ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. Ter nagedachtenis aan Prof. Dr. J. J. Duistermaat (1942–2010)

articleTitle: A Refinement of a Mixed Sparse Effective Nullstellensatz
abstract: For k ≥ n + 1 Laurent polynomials f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> in n variables which are allowed to have different Newton polytopes, we give a generically satisfied criterion under which we can find Laurent polynomials h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>, with particularly small Newton polytopes, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h_1\ f_1 +\ \cdot \cdot \cdot\ +h_k\ f_k = 1$</tex>. This gives a refinement of a result of Canny and Emiris.

articleTitle: Weighted Distribution of the 4-rank of Class Groups and Applications
abstract: We prove that the distribution of the values of the 4-rank of ideal class groups of quadratic fields is not affected when it is weighted by a divisor type function. We then give several applications concerning a new lower bound of the sums of class numbers of real quadratic fields with discriminant less than a bound tending to infinity and several questions of P. Sarnak concerning reciprocal geodesics.

articleTitle: Some Notes on Tsuzuki’s Full Faithfulness Conjecture
abstract: In this note, we will give a counter example of Tsuzuki’s fully faithfulness conjecture and propose a modified conjecture. We also propose a weaker conjecture, and prove that this conjecture is sufficient for our final goal, which is the full faithfulness conjecture of overconvergent isocrystals.

articleTitle: Local Rigidity of Partially Hyperbolic Actions. II: The Geometric Method and Restrictions of Weyl Chamber Flows on SL(n, ℝ)/Γ
abstract: We prove local differentiable rigidity for generic rank 2 restrictions of Weyl chamber flows by introducing a new “geometric” method in rigidity of actions of higher rank abelian groups based on the study of the combinatorial structure of the web of Lyapunov foliations.

articleTitle: The Gauss Map of Minimal Surfaces in the Heisenberg Group
abstract: We study the Gauss map of minimal surfaces in the Heisenberg group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Nil}_3$</tex> endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. We prove that the Gauss map of a nowhere vertical minimal surface is harmonic into the hyperbolic plane ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Conversely, any nowhere antiholomorphic harmonic map into ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is the Gauss map of a nowhere vertical minimal surface. Finally, we study the image of the Gauss map of complete nowhere vertical minimal surfaces.

articleTitle: Focusing NLS Equation: Long-Time Dynamics of Step-Like Initial Data
abstract: We consider the initial value problem for the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with “step-like” initial data: q(x, 0) = 0 for x ≤ 0 and q(x, 0) = Aexp(−2iBx) for x > 0, where A > 0 and B ∈ ℝ are constants. The paper aims at studying the long-time asymptotics of the solution to this problem. We show that there are three regions in the half-plane −∞ < x < ∞, t > 0, where the asymptotics has qualitatively different forms: a slowly decaying self-similar wave of Zakharov–Manakov type for x < −4Bt, a modulated elliptic wave for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-4Bt< x < -4(B - A\sqrt{2})t$</tex>, and a plane wave for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x > -4(B - A\sqrt{2})t$</tex>. The main tool is the asymptotic analysis of an associated matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem.

articleTitle: Entropy of Semiclassical Measures for Symplectic Linear Maps of the Multidimensional Torus
abstract: For a linear symplectic map A of the 2d-torus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb T^{2d}$</tex>, one can associate a sequence of unitary matrices <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M_N(A))_{N\in \mathbb N}$</tex> acting on Hilbert spaces of dimension N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>. The eigenstates of this sequence of matrices are said to be the stationary states of the quantum system. In this paper, we give quantitative properties on the distribution of these stationary states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb T^{2d}$</tex> in the so-called semiclassical limit (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbar =(2\pi\ N)^1\ \rightarrow\ 0$</tex>). To do this, we use semiclassical measures that are A-invariant probability measures associated to these sequences of states and we give a lower bound for the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of these measures. Our main result is that, for any quantizable matrix A in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Sp}(2d,\ \mathbb Z)$</tex> and any semiclassical measure μ associated to it, the Kolmogogorov–Sinai entropy of μ with respect to A is bounded from below by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma _{\beta \in {\mathrm sp}(A)}\ {\mathrm max(log}\ |\beta| - \lambda _{\mathrm max}/2,\ 0),$</tex> where the summation is taken over the spectrum of A (counted with multiplicities) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{\mathrm max}$</tex> is the supremum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{{\mathrm log}\ |\beta |:\ \beta \in \ {\mathrm sp}(A)\}$</tex>. In particular, our result implies that if A has an eigenvalue outside the unit circle, then a semiclassical measure cannot be carried only by periodic orbits of A.

articleTitle: Non-existence of Certain Galois Representations with a Uniform Tame Inertia Weight
abstract: In this article, we prove the non-existence of certain semistable Galois representations of a number field and apply our results to some geometric problems. For example, we prove a special case of a conjecture of Rasmussen and Tamagawa, related with the finiteness of the set of isomorphism classes of abelian varieties with constrained prime power torsion.

articleTitle: Holomorphic Structures on the Quantum Projective Line
abstract: We show that much of the structure of the 2-sphere as a complex curve survives the q-deformation and has natural generalizations to the quantum 2-sphere—which, with additional structures, we identify with the quantum projective line. Notably among these is the identification of a quantum homogeneous coordinate ring with the coordinate ring of the quantum plane. In parallel with the fact that positive Hochschild cocycles on the algebra of smooth functions on a compact oriented 2-dimensional manifold encode the information for complex structures on the surface, we formulate a notion of twisted positivity for twisted Hochschild and cyclic cocycles and exhibit an explicit twisted positive Hochschild cocycle for the complex structure on the sphere.

articleTitle: Approximation Results for Reflectionless Jacobi Matrices
abstract: We study spaces of reflectionless Jacobi matrices. The main theme is the following type of question: Given a reflectionless Jacobi matrix, is it possible to approximate it by other reflectionless and, typically, simpler Jacobi matrices of a special type? For example, can we approximate by periodic operators?

articleTitle: Genus Bounds for Harmonic Group Actions on Finite Graphs
abstract: This paper develops graph analogs of the genus bounds for the maximal size of an automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus g≥2. Inspired by the work of Baker and Norine on harmonic morphisms between finite graphs, we motivate and define the notion of a harmonic group action. Denoting by M(g) the maximal size of such a harmonic group action on a graph of genus g≥2, we prove that 4(g−1)≤M(g)≤6(g−1), and these bounds are sharp in the sense that both are attained for infinitely many values of g. Moreover, we show that the values 4(g−1) and 6(g−1) are the only values taken by the function M(g).

articleTitle: Overdetermined Boundary Value Problems for the ∞-Laplacian
abstract: We consider overdetermined boundary value problems for the ∞-Laplacian in a domain Ω of ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and discuss what kind of implications on the geometry of Ω the existence of a solution may have. The classical ∞-Laplacian, the normalized or game-theoretic ∞-Laplacian, and the limit of the p-Laplacian as p →∞are considered and provide different answers, even if we restrict our domains to those that have only web-functions as solutions.

articleTitle: On Residual Cohomology Classes Attached to Relative Rank One Eisenstein Series for the Symplectic Group
abstract: The cohomology of an arithmetically defined subgroup of the symplectic ℚ-group Sp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is closely related to the theory of automorphic forms. This paper gives a structural account of that part of the cohomology, which is generated by residues or derivatives of Eisenstein series of relative rank one. In particular, we determine a set of conditions subject to which residues of Eisenstein series may give rise to non-vanishing cohomology classes. A non-vanishing condition on the value at s = 1/2 of certain automorphic L-functions, which naturally appear in the constant terms of the Eisenstein series, plays a major role.

articleTitle: On Degree-0 Elliptic Orbifold Gromov–Witten Invariants
abstract: We compute, by two methods, the genus-1 degree-0 orbifold Gromov–Witten invariants with non-stacky insertions which are exceptional cases of the dilaton and divisor equations. One method involves a detailed analysis of the relevant moduli spaces. The other method, valid in the presence of torus actions with isolated fixed points, is virtual localization. Our computations verify the conjectural evaluations of these invariants. Some genus-1 twisted orbifold Gromov–Witten invariants are also computed.

articleTitle: On Intersections of Certain Partitions of a Group Compactification
abstract: Let G be a connected semi-simple algebraic group of adjoint type over an algebraically closed field and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar G$</tex> be the wonderful compactification of G. For a fixed pair (B,B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>) of opposite Borel subgroups of G, we look at intersections of Lusztig’s G-stable pieces and the B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>×B-orbits in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar G$</tex>, as well as intersections of B×B-orbits and B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>×B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>-orbits in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar G$</tex>. We give explicit conditions for such intersections to be nonempty, and in each case, we show that every nonempty intersection is smooth and irreducible, that the closure of the intersection is equal to the intersection of the closures, and that the nonempty intersections form a strongly admissible partition of Ḡ.

articleTitle: Counting Invariant of Perverse Coherent Sheaves and its Wall-crossing
abstract: We introduce moduli spaces of stable perverse coherent systems on small crepant resolutions of Calabi–Yau 3-folds and consider their Donaldson–Thomas-type counting invariants. The stability depends on the choice of a component ( = a chamber) in the complement of finitely many lines ( = walls) in the plane. We determine all walls and compute generating functions of invariants for all choices of chambers when the Calabi–Yau is the resolved conifold. For suitable choices of chambers, our invariants are specialized to Donaldson–Thomas, Pandharipande–Thomas and Szendroi invariants.

articleTitle: Local Statistical Properties of Schmidt Eigenvalues of Bipartite Entanglement for a Random Pure State
abstract: Consider the model of bipartite entanglement for a random pure state emerging in quantum information and quantum chaos, corresponding to the fixed trace Laguerre unitary ensemble (LUE) in random matrix theory. We focus on correlation functions of Schmidt eigenvalues for the model and prove universal limits of the correlation functions in the bulk and also at the soft and hard edges of the spectrum, as that of LUE. Further, we consider the bounded trace LUE and obtain the same universal limits.

articleTitle: Improving Roth's Theorem in the Primes
abstract: Let A be a subset of the primes. Let δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf>(N) = |{n ≤ N : n ∈ A}|/|{n ≤ N : n prime}|. We prove that if δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf>(N) ≥ C(log log log N)/(log log N)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sup> for N ≥ N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where C and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> are absolute constants, then A ∩ [1, N] contains a non-trivial three-term arithmetic progression. This improves on Green's result [4], which needs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta_P(N)\geq C'\sqrt{\log \log \log \log \log\ N}/\sqrt{\log \log \log \log\ N}$</tex>.

We bound the j-invariant of S-integral points on arbitrary modular curves over arbitrary number fields, in terms of the congruence group defining the curve, assuming a certain Runge condition is satisfied by our objects. We then apply our bounds to prove that for sufficiently large prime p, the points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^+_0(p^r)(\mathbb Q)$</tex> with r < 1 are either cusps or complex multiplication points. This can be interpreted as the non-existence of quadratic elliptic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q$</tex>-curves with higher prime-power degree.

articleTitle: Cohomology of Hyperplane Complements with Group Ring Coefficients
abstract: We compute the cohomology with group ring coefficients of the complement of a finite collection of affine hyperplanes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm C}^n$</tex>. It is nonzero in exactly one degree, namely, the degree equal to the rank of the arrangement.

articleTitle: Toward a Generalization of the Gross–Zagier Conjecture
abstract: We review some of Kolyvagin’s results and conjectures about elliptic curves and then make a new conjecture that slightly refines Kolyvagin’s conjectures. We introduce a definition of finite index subgroups W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> ⊂ E(K), one for each prime p that is inert in a fixed imaginary quadratic field K. These subgroups generalize the group ℤy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> generated by the Heegner point y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> ∈ E(K) in the case r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">an</inf> = 1. For any curve with r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">an</inf> ≥ 1, we give a description of W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, which is conditional on truth of the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and our conjectural refinement of Kolyvagin’s conjecture. We then deduce the following conditional theorems, up to an explicit finite set of primes: (1) the set of indexes [E(K) : W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>] is finite and (2) the subgroups W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> with [E(K) : W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>] maximal satisfy a higher-rank generalization of the Gross–Zagier formula. We also investigate a higher-rank generalization of a conjecture of Gross–Zagier.

articleTitle: Boundary Values and Boundary Uniqueness of J-Holomorphic Mappings
abstract: We establish a Fatou-type theorem for J-holomorphic mappings that are bounded in an appropriate sense and prove the Blaschke condition for their zero sets. We also prove a Privalov-type uniqueness theorem for pairs of J-holomorphic mappings.

articleTitle: A Selberg Trace Formula for Non-unitary Twists
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X = \Gamma \setminus G/K$</tex> be a compact locally symmetric space. In this paper, we establish a version of the Selberg trace formula for non-unitary representations of the lattice Γ. On the spectral side appears the spectrum of the “flat Laplacian” Δ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">#</sup>, acting in the space of sections of the associated flat bundle. In general, this is a non-self-adjoint operator.

articleTitle: On the Reduction of Points on Abelian Varieties and Tori
abstract: Let G be the product of an abelian variety and a torus defined over a number field K. Let R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> be points in G(K). Let ℓ be a rational prime, and let a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> be nonnegative integers. Consider the set of primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak p$</tex> of K satisfying the following condition: the ℓ-adic valuation of the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_i\ {\mathrm mod}\ \mathfrak p)$</tex> equals a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> for every i = 1, …, n. We show that this set is either finite or has a positive natural density. We characterize the n-tuples a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> for which the density is positive. More generally, we study the ℓ-part of the reduction of the points.

In this paper, we describe noncommutative versions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1 \times \mathbb P^1$</tex>. These contain the class of noncommutative deformations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1 \times \mathbb P^1$</tex>.

articleTitle: Intersection Numbers for Twisted Cycles and the Connection Problem Associated with the Generalized Hypergeometric Function n+1Fn
abstract: Connection matrices associated with the generalized hypergeometric function <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> are determined by using the intersection number of twisted cycles.

We observe that the Poincaré duality isomorphism for a string manifold is an isomorphism of modules over the subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A(2)$</tex> of the modulo 2 Steenrod algebra. In particular, the pattern of the operations Sq<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, Sq<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and Sq<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> on the cohomology of a string manifold has a symmetry around the middle dimension. We characterize this kind of cohomology operation duality in terms of the annihilator of the Thom class of the negative tangent bundle, and in terms of the vanishing of top-degree cohomology operations. We also indicate how the existence of such an operation-preserving duality implies the integrality of certain polynomials in the Pontryagin classes of the manifold.

Birman, Wenzl[3], and independently Murakami[19] introduced a class of finite dimensional algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak B_n$</tex>, which are known as the Birman–Murakami–Wenzl algebras or BMWalgebras. When the ground field κ contains invertible r and q such that o(q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), the multiplicative order of q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, is strictly greater than n, and char(κ), the characteristic of κ is not 2, we determine the structure of the cell module Δ(1, λ) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak B_n$</tex>, where λ is any partition of n −2. In particular, we compute the dimension of the simple head of Δ(1, λ). Cox, De Visscher, and Martin have classified the blocks of Brauer algebras B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> in characteristic zero[5]. We solve the similar problem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak B_n$</tex> over the aforementioned field κ. As a by-product, we give a criterion for each module of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak B_n$</tex> being equal to its simple head over an arbitrary field.

articleTitle: Closure of Steinberg Fibers and Affine Deligne–Lusztig Varieties
abstract: We discuss some connections between the closure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar F$</tex> of a Steinberg fiber in the wonderful compactification of an adjoint group and the affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>(1) in the affine flag variety. Among other things, we describe the emptiness/nonemptiness pattern of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>(1) if the translation part of w is quasi-regular. As a by-product, we give a new proof of the explicit description of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar F$</tex>, first obtained in He [“Unipotent variety in the group compactification.” Advances in Mathematics 203 (2006): 109–31].

articleTitle: Modular Frobenius Manifolds and their Invariant Flows
abstract: The space of Frobenius manifolds has a natural involutive symmetry on it: there exists a map I which sends a Frobenius manifold to another Frobenius manifold. Also, from a Frobenius manifold one may construct a so-called almost dual Frobenius manifold which satisfies almost all of the axioms of a Frobenius manifold. The action of I on the almost dual manifolds is studied, and the action of I on objects such as periods, twisted periods, and flows is studied. A distinguished class of Frobenius manifolds sit at the fixed point of this involutive symmetry, and this is made manifest in certain modular properties of the various structures. In particular, up to a simple reciprocal transformation, for this class of modular Frobenius manifolds, the flows are invariant under the action of I.

The Camassa–Holm (CH) equation describes pseudo-spherical surfaces and therefore its integrability properties can be studied by geometrical means [Reyes, “Geometric integrability of the Camassa–Holm equation.” Letters in Mathematical Physics 59 (2002): 117–31]. Using this fact, we introduce a “Miura transform” and a “modified” Camassa–Holm (mCH) equation, in analogy with the Korteweg–de Vries theory. We obtain an infinite number of local conservation laws for CH from these data and also an infinite number of (non)local symmetries. We then compute conservation laws for mCH and also show that it describes pseudo-spherical surfaces, so that, in particular, it is the integrability condition of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$sl(2,\ \mathbb R)$</tex>-valued linear problem. Finally, we investigate mCH analytically: we define weak solutions and prove their existence and uniqueness.

An origami manifold is a manifold equipped with a closed 2-form which is symplectic except on a hypersurface, where it is like the pullback of a symplectic form by a folding map and its kernel fibrates with oriented circle fibers over a compact base. We can move back and forth between origami and symplectic manifolds using cutting (unfolding) and radial blow-up (folding), modulo compatibility conditions. We prove an origami convexity theorem for Hamiltonian torus actions, classify toric origami manifolds by polyhedral objects resembling paper origami and discuss examples. We also prove a cobordism result and compute the cohomology of a special class of origami manifolds.

articleTitle: An Example of a Topologically Non-rigid Foliation of the Complex projective plane
abstract: We give here an explicit example of an algebraic family of foliations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb CP^2$</tex> which is topologically trivial but not analytically trivial. This example underlines the necessity of some assumptions in Y. Ilyashenko’s rigidity theorem.

articleTitle: On a Quantum Analog of the Caldero–Chapoton Formula
abstract: Let Q be any valued quiver without oriented cycles. We study connections between the category of valued representations of Q and expansions of cluster variables in terms of an initial cluster in quantum cluster algebras. We show that an analog of the Caldero–Chapoton formula holds for the specializations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q=|\mathbb F|$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F$</tex> is a finite field, in all quantum cluster algebras of finite type, including nonsimply laced types, and for any cluster variable in an almost acyclic cluster.

We give a proof that the Riemann hypothesis for hypersurfaces over finite fields implies the result for all smooth proper varieties, by a deformation argument which does not use the theory of Lefschetz pencils or the ℓ-adic Fourier transform.

articleTitle: Hypergeometric Formulas for Lattice Sums and Mahler Measures
abstract: In this paper, we will prove several formulas relating hypergeometric functions to lattice sums with four indices of summation. These results are related to Boyd’s conjectured identities between Mahler measures and special values of L-series of elliptic curves.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Stationary Phase Method for Oscillatory Riemann–Hilbert Problems
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of oscillatory Riemann–Hilbert problems (RHPs) arising in the Ablowitz-Kaup-Newell-Segur hierarchy of integrable nonlinear partial differential equations. Our method is based on the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method in which the given RHP localizes to small neighborhoods of stationary phase points. In their original work, Deift and Zhou only considered analytic phase functions. Subsequently, Varzugin extended the Deift–Zhou method to a certain restricted class of nonanalytic phase functions. In this paper, we extend Varzugin’s method to a substantially more general class of nonanalytic phase functions. In our work, real variable methods play a key role.

articleTitle: Growth of Small Generating Sets in SLn(ℤ/pℤ)
abstract: Let G=SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and fix δ a positive number. We prove that there are positive numbers ϵ and C such that, for all fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K=\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$</tex> (p prime), and all sets A⊂G(K) that generate G(K), either |A|>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1−δ</sup>, δ>0 or |A⋅A⋅A|≥C|A|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1+ϵ</sup>.

articleTitle: Tensor Products, Characters, and Blocks of Finite-Dimensional Representations of Quantum Affine Algebras at Roots of Unity
abstract: We establish several results concerning tensor products, q-characters, and the block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional representations of quantum affine algebras in the root of unity setting. In the generic case, a Weyl module is isomorphic to a tensor product of fundamental representations and this isomorphism was essential for establishing the block decomposition theorem. This is no longer true in the root of unity setting. We overcome the lack of such a tool by utilizing results on specialization of modules. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition for a Weyl module to be a tensor product of fundamental representations and prove that this condition is also necessary when the underlying simple Lie algebra is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak sl_2$</tex>. We also study the braid group invariance of q-characters of fundamental representations.

We show that sequences of unit-volume compact gradient Ricci solitons converge to complete orbifold gradient solitons, assuming constraints on the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n/2</sup>-norm of curvature, the soliton constant λ, and the auxiliary constant C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. The strongest results are in dimension 4, where L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> curvature bounds are equivalent to bounds on the Euler number, given the other constraints. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for limits to be compact.

articleTitle: C1, α Regularity for Solutions to the p-harmonic Thin Obstacle Problem
abstract: We prove C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1, α</sup> regularity for a thin obstacle problem for the p-Laplace equation. Due to the non-linearity of the p-Laplace operator, we cannot use the same methods used for the Laplace case, instead we use techniques developed by E. de Giorgi.

articleTitle: On the Drinfeld–Sokolov Hierarchies of D Type
abstract: We extend the notion of pseudo-differential operators that are used to represent the Gelfand–Dickey hierarchies and obtain a similar representation for the full Drinfeld–Sokolov hierarchies of D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> type. By using such pseudo-differential operators, we introduce the tau functions of these bihamiltonian hierarchies and prove that these hierarchies are equivalent to the integrable hierarchies defined by Date–Jimbo–Kashiware–Miwa and Kac–Wakimoto from the basic representation of the Kac–Moody algebra D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>.

We introduce the notions of normal tensor functor and exact sequence of tensor categories. We show that exact sequences of tensor categories generalize strictly exact sequences of Hopf algebras as defined by Schneider, and in particular, exact sequences of (finite) groups. We classify exact sequences of tensor categories <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {C}'}\rightarrow \cal {C} \rightarrow {\cal {C}''}$</tex> (such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {C}'}$</tex> is finite) in terms of normal, faithful Hopf monads on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {C}''}$</tex> and also in terms of self-trivializing commutative algebras in the center of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}$</tex>. More generally, we show that, given any dominant tensor functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}\rightarrow \cal {D}$</tex> admitting an exact (right or left) adjoint, there exists a canonical commutative algebra (A,σ) in the center of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}$</tex> such that F is tensor equivalent to the free module functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal C {\rightarrow} \mathrm {mod_{\cal C}}(A, \sigma)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm {mod_{\cal C}}(A, \sigma)$</tex> denotes the category of A-modules in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal C$</tex> endowed with a monoidal structure defined using σ. We re-interpret equivariantization under a finite group action on a tensor category and, in particular, the modularization construction, in terms of exact sequences, Hopf monads, and commutative central algebras. As an application, we prove that a braided fusion category whose dimension is odd and square-free is equivalent, as a fusion category, to the representation category of a group.

articleTitle: Real Quadratic Analogs of Traces of Singular Moduli
abstract: In this paper, regularized Petersson inner products of certain weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {3}{2}$</tex> weakly holomorphic (or harmonic) modular forms are expressed in terms of real quadratic analogs of traces of singular moduli. The proofs make use of the theory of weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {1}{2}$</tex> mock-modular forms.

articleTitle: Quantum Affine Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov Equations and Quantum Spherical Functions, I
abstract: Cherednik's quantum affine Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations associated to an affine Hecke algebra module M form a holonomic system of q-difference equations acting on M-valued functions on a complex torus T. In this paper the quantum affine Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations are related to the Cherednik–Macdonald theory when M is induced from a character of a standard parabolic subalgebra of the affine Hecke algebra. We set up correspondences between solutions of the quantum affine KZ equations and, on the one hand, solutions to the spectral problem of the Cherednik–Dunkl q-difference reflection operators (generalizing work of Kasatani and Takeyama) and, on the other hand, solutions to the spectral problem of the Cherednik–Macdonald q-difference operators (generalizing work of Cherednik). The correspondences are applicable to all relevant spaces of functions on T and for all parameter values, including the cases that q and/or the Hecke algebra parameters are roots of unity.

Let p(n) denote the partition function. In this article, we will show that congruences of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\qquad$$</tex> exist for all primes m and ℓ satisfying m≥13 and ℓ≠2,3,m, where B is a suitably chosen integer depending on m and ℓ. Here, the integer k depends on the Hecke eigenvalues of a certain invariant subspace of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m/2−1</inf>(Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(576),χ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>) and can be explicitly computed. More generally, we will show that for each integer i>0 there exists an integer k such that with a properly chosen B the congruence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$p(m^i\ell ^kn\ + B) \equiv 0\ {\mathrm mod}\ m^i$$</tex> holds for all integers n not divisible by ℓ.

articleTitle: A Uniform Strong Spectral Gap for Congruence Covers of a Compact Quotient of PSL(2, ℝ)d
abstract: The existence of a strong spectral gap for lattices in semi–simple Lie groups is crucial in many applications. In particular, for arithmetic lattices, it is useful to have bounds for the strong spectral gap that are uniform in the family of congruence covers. When the lattice is itself a congruence group, there are uniform and very good bounds for the spectral gap coming from the known bounds toward the Ramanujan–Selberg conjectures. In this note, we establish a uniform bound for the strong spectral gap for congruence covers of an irreducible co-compact lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm PSL}(2, \mathbb R)^d$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq2$</tex>, which is the simplest and most basic case where the congruence subgroup property is not known.

articleTitle: The Fine Moduli Space of Representations of Clifford Algebras
abstract: Given a fixed binary form f(u,v) of degree d over a field k, the associated Clifford algebra is the k-algebra C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>=k{u,v}/I, where I is the two-sided ideal generated by elements of the form (αu+βv)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>−f(α,β) with α and β arbitrary elements in k. All representations of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> have dimensions that are multiples of d, and occur in families. In this article, we construct fine moduli spaces U=U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f,r</inf> for the irreducible rd-dimensional representations of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> for each r≥2. Our construction starts with the projective curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C\subset \mathbb P^2_k$</tex> defined by the equation w<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>=f(u,v), and produces U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f,r</inf> as a quasiprojective variety in the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal M(r,\ d_r)$</tex> of stable vector bundles over C with rank r and degree d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=r(d+g−1), where g denotes the genus of C.

articleTitle: Sobolev Mappings: Lipschitz Density is not an Isometric Invariant of the Target
abstract: If M is a compact smooth manifold and X is a compact metric space, then the Sobolev space W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,p</sup>(M,X) is defined through an isometric embedding of X into a Banach space. We prove that the answer to the question whether Lipschitz mappings Lip (M,X) are dense in W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,p</sup>(M,X) may depend on the isometric embedding of the target.

articleTitle: Supercritical Conformal Metrics on Surfaces with Conical Singularities
abstract: We study the problem of prescribing the Gaussian curvature on surfaces with conical singularities in supercritical regimes. Using a Morse-theoretical approach, we prove a general existence theorem on surfaces with positive genus, with a generic multiplicity result.

articleTitle: Singular Hermitian–Einstein Monopoles on the Product of a Circle and a Riemann Surface
abstract: In this paper, the moduli space of singular unitary Hermitian–Einstein monopoles on the product of a circle and a Riemann surface is shown to correspond to a moduli space of stable pairs on the Riemann surface. These pairs consist of a holomorphic vector bundle on the surface and a meromorphic automorphism of the bundle. The singularities of this automorphism correspond to the singularities of the singular monopole. We then consider the complex geometry of the moduli space; in particular, we compute dimensions, both from the complex geometric and the gauge theoretic point of view.

articleTitle: On Goncharov’s Regulator and Higher Arithmetic Chow Groups
abstract: In this paper, we show that the regulator defined by Goncharov in [10] from higher algebraic Chow groups to Deligne–Beilinson cohomology agrees with Beilinson’s regulator. We give a direct comparison of Goncharov’s regulator to the construction given by Burgos Gil and Feliu in [5]. As a consequence, we show that the higher arithmetic Chow groups defined by Goncharov agree, for all projective arithmetic varieties over an arithmetic field, with the ones defined by Burgos Gil and Feliu.

articleTitle: On the Fluctuations of Matrix Elements of the Quantum Cat Map
abstract: We study the fluctuations of the diagonal matrix elements of the quantum cat map about their limit. We show that after suitable normalization, the fifth centered moment for the Hecke basis vanishes in the semiclassical limit, confirming in part a conjecture of Kurlberg and Rudnick. We also study sums of matrix elements lying in short windows. For observables with zero mean, the first moment of these sums is zero, and the variance was determined by the author along with Kurlberg and Rudnick. We show that if the window is sufficiently small in terms of Planck’s constant, then the third moment vanishes if we normalize so that the variance is of order 1.

articleTitle: Line Bundles on Totally Degenerated Formal Schemes
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of smooth rigid analytic varieties X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> over a complete non-Archimedean field K; namely those which have a totally degenerated formal model; that is, a strict semi-stable model X over the valuation ring R of K such that the irreducible components of the special fiber X⊗<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>k are rational varieties. These are natural generalizations of the well known Mumford curves to arbitrary dimension. In these cases, the Picard variety reflects nicely the combinatorics of the special fiber. Similar to the one-dimensional case, we will show that the Picard variety of these varieties is given by a quotient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb G^g_{m,K}/M$</tex>, where M is a lattice in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb G^g_{m,K}$</tex>, not necessarily of full rank.
In this paper we prove the existence of absolutely dicritical foliations for any configuration of exceptional divisor.

articleTitle: Fluctuations in Random Complex Zeroes: Asymptotic Normality Revisited
abstract: The Gaussian Entire Function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\begin{equation*} {F(z)=\displaystyle {\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}} \zeta_{k} z^{k} \over \sqrt{k!}} \end{equation*}</tex> (ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>,ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,… are Gaussian i.i.d. complex random coefficients) is distinguished by the distribution invariance of its zero set with respect to the isometries of the complex plane. We find close to optimal conditions on a function h that yield asymptotic normality of linear statistics of zeroes<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$n(R,\displaystyle h)={\sum_{a:F(a)=0}} {h}({{a}\over {R}})$$</tex>when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \rightarrow \infty$</tex>, and construct examples of function h with abnormal fluctuations of linear statistics. We show that the fluctuations of n(R,h) are asymptotically normal when h is either a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\alpha }_{0}$</tex>-function with α>1, or a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\alpha }_{0}$</tex>-function with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \leq {1}$</tex> such that the variance of n(R,h) is at least R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2α+ε</sup> with some ε>0.These results complement our recent results from “Clustering of correlation functions for random complex zeroes”, where, using different methods, we prove that the fluctuations of n(R,h) are asymptotically normal when h is bounded, and the variance of n(R,h) grows at least as a positive power of R.

articleTitle: Felder’s Elliptic Quantum Group and Elliptic Hypergeometric Series on the Root System An
abstract: We introduce a generalization of elliptic 6j-symbols, which can be interpreted as matrix elements for intertwiners between corepresentations of Felder’s elliptic quantum group. For special parameter values, they can be expressed in terms of multivariable elliptic hypergeometric series related to the root system A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. As a consequence, we obtain new biorthogonality relations for such series.

articleTitle: Higher-order Analogues of the Slice Genus of a Knot
abstract: For certain classes of knots, we define geometric invariants called higher-order genera. Each of these invariants is a refinement of the slice genus of a knot. We find lower bounds for the higher-order genera in terms of certain von Neumann ρ-invariants, which we call higher-order signatures. The higher-order genera offer a refinement of the Grope filtration of the knot concordance group.

In this paper, we discuss the existence problem of Sasakian–Einstein metric. By introducing two transverse holomorphic invariants, we obtain Harnack type inequalities for transverse Monge–Ampère equation, and an existence result for Sasakian–Einstein metric.

articleTitle: The Langlands–Kottwitz approach for the modular curve
abstract: We show how the Langlands–Kottwitz method can be used to determine the local factors of the Hasse–Weil zeta-function of the modular curve at places of bad reduction. On the way, we prove a conjecture of Haines and Kottwitz in this special case.

articleTitle: Anticyclotomic p-adic L-function of Central Critical Rankin–Selberg L-value
abstract: Let M be an imaginary quadratic field, f a Hecke eigen-cusp form on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm GL}_2(\mathbb Q)\setminus {\mathrm GL}_2(\mathbb A)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat \pi_{\mathrm f}$</tex> the unitary base-change to M of automorphic representation π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> associated to f. Take a unitary arithmetic Hecke character χ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^\times\setminus M^\times_\mathbb A$</tex> inducing the inverse of the central character of π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>. The celebrated formula of Waldspurger relates the square of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L\chi\ ({\mathrm f}):=\int _{M^\times\setminus M^\times_\mathbb A}{\mathrm f}(t)\chi(t)d^\times t$</tex> to the central critical value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(\frac {1}{2},\ \hat \pi_{\mathrm f}\ \otimes\ \chi)$</tex>. We construct a new p-adic L-function that interpolates L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">χ</inf>(f) over arithmetic χ's for a cusp form f in the spirit of the landmark result of Katz where he did that for the Eisenstein series.

articleTitle: A Special Case of a Conjecture by Widom with Implications to Fermionic Entanglement Entropy
abstract: We prove a special case of a conjecture in asymptotic analysis by Harold Widom. More precisely, we establish the leading and next-to-leading term of a semiclassical expansion of the trace of the square of certain integral operators on the Hilbert space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2(\mathbb R^d)$</tex>. As already observed by Gioev and Klich, this implies that the bipartite entanglement entropy of the free Fermi gas in its ground state grows at least as fast as the surface area of the spatially bounded part times a logarithmic enhancement.

articleTitle: On Certain Automorphic Descents to GL2
abstract: We consider a new construction of automorphic representations of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(A), using the general idea of automorphic descent methods. In particular, four families of examples are considered. The representations τ of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(A) are obtained from automorphic representations π on reductive groups H, which contain a reductive subgroup G of GSp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</inf>. We give criteria for nonvanishing and for cuspidality of the constructed representations τ, in terms of periods or co-periods and by the holomorphy at s=1 of certain l-functions of π. We also calculate the relation of the unramified parameters in certain cases, which indicates that τ and π fit partially to the Langlands functorial principle. We prove some low-rank cases to support our conjectures.

We provide a family of counterexamples to a first formulation of the dynamical Manin–Mumford conjecture. We propose a revision of this conjecture and prove it for arbitrary subvarieties of Abelian varieties under the action of group endomorphisms and for lines under the action of diagonal endomorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$</tex>.

articleTitle: Liftability of Mod p Cusp Forms of Parallel Weights
abstract: We present a vanishing theorem for automorphic line bundles on good reduction fibers of PEL-type Shimura varieties (including all noncompact ones). As a consequence, we deduce that for a good prime p no smaller than the dimension of a PEL-type Shimura variety, any mod p cusp form of positive cohomological parallel weight is liftable to characteristic zero.

articleTitle: Weak Density of the Fundamental Group Scheme
abstract: Let X be a nonsingular projective variety over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi^{\mathrm et}_1\ (X)\ = 0$</tex>, then for any ample line bundle H on X, any semistable bundle E on X with all Chern classes 0 is trivial. Over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C$</tex>, this a consequence of the fact that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi ^{\mathrm top}_1\ (X_{\mathrm an})$</tex> is a finitely generated group and hence any representation into a linear group is residually finite. We prove an analog of this theorem in characteristic p>0. Semistable bundles with vanishing Chern classes are replaced by Nori semistable bundles, that is those which are semistable of degree 0 on any curve mapping to X. The étale fundamental group is replaced by Nori’s fundamental group scheme π<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>(X) [Nori, M. “The fundamental group-scheme.” Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences, Mathematical Sciences 91 no. 2 (1982), 73–122], which is the profinite completion of the tensor automorphism group scheme π<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup>(X) of Nori semistable bundles [Langer, A. “On the S-Fundamental group scheme II,” (2009): preprint] studied by Langer [“On the S-Fundamental group scheme,” preprint arXiv/0905.4600;“On the S-Fundamental group scheme II,” (2009): preprint].

We define and study categories of singular Soergel bimodules, which are certain natural generalizations of Soergel bimodules. Indecomposable singular Soergel bimodules are classified, and we conclude that the split Grothendieck group of the 2-category of singular Soergel bimodules is isomorphic to the Schur algebroid. Soergel’s conjecture on the characters of indecomposable Soergel bimodules in characteristic zero is shown to imply a similar conjecture for the characters of singular Soergel bimodules.

We present an explicit difference operator diagonalized by the Macdonald polynomials associated with an (arbitrary) admissible pair of irreducible reduced crystallographic root systems. By the duality symmetry, this gives rise to an explicit Pieri formula for the Macdonald polynomials in question. The simplest examples of our construction recover Macdonald's celebrated difference operators and associated Pieri formulas pertaining to the minuscule and quasi-minuscule weights. As further by-products, explicit expansions, and Littlewood–Richardson type formulas are obtained for the Macdonald polynomials associated with a special class of small weights.
